prompts:
Use case: identity-preserve.
Asset type: seven-part transparent layered-character artwork atlas for Unity 2D mesh skinning. The input is the APPROVED assembled front master; preserve its exact adult face, body proportions, garment silhouettes, folds and pale warm colors. This is a decomposition of that master, not a redesign.
Create exactly SEVEN isolated pieces on one spacious square transparent sheet at ONE COMMON DRAWING SCALE. Do not resize each piece to fill its own space. The whole head should be about one third the height of a complete leg and under half the height of the torso/pelvis piece; keep the original 6.5–7-head adult proportions. Match the reference's fine warm linework and light clear painted shading.
PARTS AND LAYOUT:
1. TOP CENTER: the same complete head WITH a naturally painted full neck continuing below the jaw, same short dark-brown hair, original ordinary adult face and mildly worried neutral expression, no glasses. Only head and neck, no shirt collar. The neck must extend far enough to tuck inside/behind the torso's collar. Small relative to the other parts; head+neck approximately 250px high when a full leg is~800px high.
2. CENTER: ONE continuous torso AND pelvis, from the open shirt collar and vest shoulders through the original belt and trouser crotch/upper hip area. Keep ivory shirt, plain open gray-brown vest, original button positions and front folds, rectangular belt buckle, and uninterrupted waist connection. No head, no arms, no complete legs, no pouch. Complete the hidden shirt/vest under both arm roots and hidden trouser fabric under the pouch. Continue the pelvis's trouser fabric a short way into each leg root for overlap; NO black horizontal lines or new hems across the thigh cuts, NO shorts cuffs. Approximate size350px wide by600px high.
3. LEFT SIDE beside the torso: character's anatomical RIGHT arm, one COMPLETE CONTINUOUS ARM from rounded sleeve shoulder through the rolled elbow sleeve, bare forearm and relaxed full hand. Preserve its exact original front-view pose, length, gentle angle and clothing folds. Do NOT cut at the elbow or wrist. No flat elbow disk, no extra cuff on the bare forearm, no separate hand. Approximate size170px wide by600px high.
4. RIGHT SIDE beside torso: anatomical LEFT complete arm, same rules, faithfully matched to the other arm and the source. No pocket pose. Same common scale.
5. BOTTOM LEFT: anatomical RIGHT entire trouser leg WITH its original low brown lace-up shoe, from hidden upper thigh/hip attachment through knee to sole, ONE continuous piece. Match the source's leg length and folds. Do NOT cut at knee or ankle. Extend the upper trouser fabric behind the pelvis by 40–60px of soft fabric overlap, no exposed flesh/cross-section, no horizontal seam drawn across its top. Approximate size220px wide by800px high.
6. BOTTOM RIGHT: anatomical LEFT entire leg plus shoe, same rules and common scale, preserve its source-specific folds. Both full legs should be equal adult length and shoes stay the same scale as the reference.
7. SMALL separate pouch at FAR RIGHT LOWER EMPTY AREA: the original brown drawstring coin pouch with its short attachment loop. No extra money, no new props. Keep its source size, only about110px high, not enlarged.
The two arms should each be roughly the height of the torso/pelvis piece; each leg is taller than the torso/pelvis; the head+neck is much shorter than torso. Keep limbs and torso at a shared consistent pixel scale so an adult with the input proportions can be reconstructed.
Show only these seven isolated flat-painted parts with generous TRANSPARENT gaps (at least40px at intended2048x2048 scale) and full unclipped margins. Keep the atlas approximately2048x2048 and use space freely. Underlap roots are plain continued skin or fabric that will be hidden after assembly; they are NOT anatomical amputation disks or outlined cut edges. No labels, no numbers, no diagram lines, no assembled preview figure, no extra expressions, no spare limb fragments, no chibi/SD proportions, no crop marks, no grid, no borders, no shadows, no background or glow. TRUE transparent RGBA background.
Critical: clean complete neck, waist already connected, elbows already connected, knees already connected. Do not introduce separate upper/lower arms, thighs/shins, or a detached belt. Reconstruct hidden overlap material while retaining the exact identity and original cohesive drawing.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit target: the seven-part character atlas. Make ONE layout-only change: move the small brown drawstring coin pouch from the lower-right area to the large EMPTY LOWER CENTER area, centered at about 50% of canvas width and 86% of canvas height (below the torso/pelvis and between the two full legs). Keep the pouch at EXACTLY its current small size. This ensures it lies outside both full-leg rectangular bounding boxes and can be exported as an isolated sprite. Keep every other pixel region, all six other parts, their placement, scale, face, anatomy, original folds, colors, adult proportions, linework and transparency unchanged. Do NOT redraw or rescale the head, torso, arms or legs. There must still be exactly seven isolated parts: head+neck at top center, continuous torso+pelvis in middle, whole arms alongside torso, whole leg+shoe at each outer edge, and now the small pouch below center. Keep at least40px transparent margin around pouch and other parts. True transparent RGBA background; no labels, no background, no new objects, no outlines on joint cut edges.
